In [[algebraic topology]], several types of products are defined on homological and cohomological theories.

==The cross product==

:<math>H_p(X) \otimes H_q(Y) \to H_{p+q}(X\times Y)</math>

When ''X'' and ''Y'' are [[CW complex]]es, then the product  <math>X \times Y</math> has a natural CW structure, and the cross product can be understood as induced by the chain map sending a ''p''-cell <math> e_p </math> in ''X'' and a ''q''-cell <math> e_q </math> in ''Y'' to the product cell <math> e_p \times e_q </math> in <math>X \times Y</math>.  An equivalent but slightly more complicated definition can be given for singular homology. The cross product is used to prove the [[Künneth theorem]] relating the homology of ''X'' and ''Y'' to the homology of <math>X \times Y</math>.

==The cap product==
{{Main| Cap product}}

:<math>\frown\ : H_p(X;R)\times H^q(X;R) \rightarrow H_{p-q}(X;R)</math>

==The slant product==
{{Main|slant product}}

:<math>/ : H_p(X;R)\times H^q(X\times Y;R) \rightarrow H^{q-p}(Y;R)</math>

==The cup product==
{{Main|cup product}}

:<math>H^p(X) \otimes H^q(X) \to H^{p+q}(X)</math>

This product can be understood as induced by the exterior product of [[differential form]]s in [[de Rham cohomology]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Hutchings |first=Michael |author-link=Michael Hutchings (mathematician) |date= |title=Cup Product and Intersections |url=https://math.berkeley.edu/~hutching/teach/215b-2011/cup.pdf |archive-url= |archive-date= |access-date= |website=}}</ref> It makes the singular cohomology of a connected manifold into a unitary supercommutative ring.
